location: specs/behavioral-spec.md:10-11 (REQ-2) vs specs/behavioral-spec.md:24-25 (REQ-6); cross-ref docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-29-profitable-article-writer-design.md:229-231; also specs/verification-architecture.md:52-53 (Sprint-1 DONE)
problem: REQ-2 is an unqualified ubiquitous SHALL: 'The only permitted human contribution is COMPUTE plus a one-time payout identity supplied at install. No human click / OTP relay / approval / delivery at runtime.' REQ-6 states the DEFAULT mode (Mode A, AUTONOMY=off) 'SHALL stop at a note DRAFT and notify the human (URL + screenshot) for review; it SHALL NOT publish.' The design source is explicit that this is a genuine per-cycle runtime human action, not a one-time install fact: 'Dais reviews/edits -> Dais clicks publish. (human = final gate)' (design doc line 230-231). That is a human click at runtime for every article cycle in the default mode -- exactly what REQ-2 says is forbidden. The verification-architecture.md Sprint-1 DONE line (52-53) compounds this by asserting 'stops at Mode-A draft ... no human step' as an objective pass criterion, while the very scenario it describes (Mode-A draft awaiting Dais's click) structurally requires a human step for the article to ever go live. As written, REQ-2 and REQ-6 cannot both be simultaneously true in the shipped default configuration.
fix: Scope REQ-2 explicitly: either (a) restrict REQ-2's 'no human click at runtime' claim to Mode B only, and state in REQ-2/REQ-6 that Mode A is an intentionally human-gated bootstrap phase that does NOT satisfy REQ-2 (so REQ-2 becomes conditional on mode), or (b) redefine REQ-6's Mode A boundary so that 'runtime loop' explicitly excludes the review-to-publish click (treat it as an install-adjacent, not per-article, action) and justify why that framing is not human-in-the-runtime-loop. Update Sprint-1 DONE in verification-architecture.md to stop claiming 'no human step' for a scenario whose entire purpose is a human review gate.
